rows.title: Sharpness
rows.text: Your eyesight is much blurrier than a human's. If you are a domestic dog, a review cites an estimate of 20/75 for a typical dog, which means you must stand 20 feet from what a human can make out from 75 feet. If you are a red fox, the cells in your retina allow about 6 cycles a degree, a fifth of a human's 30, and if you are an arctic fox the estimate is about 9.
rows.note: Left out coyotes, wolves, jackals and other foxes (carried grade g) and the unmeasured species to stay within three sentences.

rows.title: Sharpest spot
rows.text: If you are a domestic dog with a long skull, as a wolf has, you see most sharply along a horizontal band level with the horizon, and if you have a short nose like a pug, you see most sharply in one spot in the middle. A red fox has a distinct spot plus a moderate band, and an Arctic fox has a distinct spot. Nobody has measured this in the other members of the dog family, so if you are a coyote, a jackal or another relative, nobody knows where your eyes see most sharply.
rows.note: Left out the Arctic fox's streak and all cell-density numbers: the Arctic fox quote states only the spot, and the numbers had no comparison job.

rows.title: Color
rows.text: You have two kinds of color-sensing cell, where a human has three. This has been measured in the domestic dog, the red fox and the arctic fox, and each has two kinds.
rows.note: Left out wavelengths (429 and 555 nm) and any claim about which colors look gray, since no record states what dogs or foxes see as gray.

rows.title: Field of view, dim light and depth
rows.text: If you are a domestic dog, a review estimates that you take in about 240 degrees around you, where a human takes in 180, and that your two eyes overlap by 30 to 60 degrees. In dim light you have more rods than a human, even in the center of the retina where a human has none, and about 7 in 10 dogs examined had a full-sized tapetum, the mirror layer behind the retina, while a few had none. Nobody has measured how well you judge depth.
rows.note: Dropped the 539 count and the 2 percent figure. The depth sentence rests on no record, because R5 is a cat record on focusing range.
